intro: We benchmarked these methods on 7 open models served by vLLM on one NVIDIA GB10 (Blackwell). Small: Llama 3.2 3B, Qwen3-4B, Ministral 3 3B. Medium: Qwen3-8B, Granite 4.2 8B, Llama 3.1 8B, Ministral 3 8B. Each method was compared with the original, unquantized model (BF16, 16-bit weights) on about 20 benchmarks. Speedup is how much faster it finished them. Size is the checkpoint as a share of the original. Quality lists only losses that were statistically significant.
terms: Ranges are across the models in each size class. Speed is throughput at 32 concurrent requests. Long answers: hundreds to thousands of output tokens. Short answers: one-letter replies, where the prompt dominates the work. Long prompts: 4k–32k-token prompts.

Quality loss
rows.small: Qwen3-4B skips tool calls (BFCL 0.880 → 0.832, p = 6e-5). Ministral 3B loses multi-turn tool use (−11.5 pp) and GSM8K reasoning (−4.1 pp) while thinking 27% longer.
rows.medium: Llama 3.1 8B writes tool calls as prose in multi-turn (p = 0.007). Ministral 8B thinks ~⅓ longer and loses 5.5 pp on GSM8K reasoning.

rows.label: Speedup by task: long answers / short answers / long prompts
Quality loss
rows.small: Qwen3-4B: code −6.4 pp, repetition loops on instruction following. Llama 3.2 3B loses retrieval at 32k. Ministral 3B: MMLU −6.0 pp, reasoning −3.5 to −4.8 pp.
rows.medium: Accuracy holds. Granite falls into tool-call loops; Qwen3-8B thinks 8.8% longer.

rows.label: Hardware
rows.small: Its 4-bit activations run only on Blackwell FP4 tensor cores, as on the benchmark's GB10. Other GPUs at best serve it as 4-bit weights only, at roughly W4A16 speed.

rows.label: Notes
rows.small: Qwen3-8B, one request at a time: time per token 72 ms → 39 ms (original) and 24 ms (FP8); 2.0–3.1 tokens accepted per step. Cost: on 4k-token prompts at 32 concurrent requests, time to first token rose from 2.9 s to 16.4 s. A stock head accepted fewer tokens on a fine-tuned Qwen3-4B (1.54–1.83 against 1.96–2.30), so train the Speculator on the final model.
